description: Compare Cloud Run, Railway TypeScript, and Railway Rust. Includes HTTP and GraphQL traffic, errors, latency, Rust gateway routes, metrics collection health, and Rust process resources. Metrics refresh every minute; rates use five-minute windows.

options.content:
**Cloud Run · Railway TypeScript · Railway Rust** — select **Backend** to filter. Refresh: **1 minute**. Timing charts use **5-minute** windows; the timing tables use the selected time range. **Operation** and **Call type** filter both operation sections.

**No traffic** means idle; missing series mean no telemetry. Rust **forward** includes TypeScript time, so do not sum both request counts. Cloud Run data is historical where available.

panels.title: HTTP success rate (5m)
panels.description: Share of observed requests without HTTP 5xx responses. No traffic means no requests in the five-minute window; it is not a synthetic uptime check.

panels.title: Request rate
panels.description: Observed requests per second across all instrumented paths. An idle backend remains at zero when metrics are arriving.

panels.title: HTTP p95
panels.description: 95th percentile of observed HTTP durations over five minutes. No traffic means a percentile cannot be calculated.

panels.title: What's running
panels.description: Live resource metadata. Rust identifies its private scrape endpoint; it does not export a deployment revision. Missing hosts have no current telemetry.

options.content:
Each row matches an **operation name + call type** over the selected time range. **Avg Δ % = (Rust / TypeScript − 1) × 100**: negative means lower observed Rust latency; positive means higher. Select **Backend → All** (or both Railway backends) to compare.

Rust avg, p95, and local calls cover only requests Rust **answered itself**. **Rust forwarded** counts requests passed whole to TypeScript, which the TypeScript columns already include; an operation Rust only forwards has no Rust timing. Calls are estimated; **No samples** means no observed counter increase. Inputs, cache states, and traffic mix differ, so this is not a controlled benchmark.

panels.title: Same-operation comparison — selected range
panels.description: Matches operationName and operationType across Railway Rust and TypeScript. Average and p95 use the same selected time range. Rust avg, Rust p95, and Rust local calls use only route="local", the requests Rust answered itself. Rust forwarded counts route="forward" requests: their time is TypeScript's plus a network hop, and the TypeScript columns already include them. Avg Δ % is 100 × (Rust average / TypeScript average − 1), calculated only when both sides have observed calls and the TypeScript average is positive. Missing sides stay No samples. Counts are extrapolated estimates. This compares aggregate traffic, not paired requests.

panels.title: Rust gateway request rate by route
panels.description: Rust /graphql requests by route: local means Rust answered the request; forward means Rust proxied the complete request to the TypeScript service.

panels.title: Rust gateway p95 by route
panels.description: Rust /graphql requests by route: local means Rust answered the request; forward means Rust proxied the complete request to the TypeScript service.

panels.title: Rust metrics scrape
panels.description: The last Alloy scrape of Rust’s private metrics port. Up confirms scraping. Down means Alloy is reporting but cannot reach Rust. No recent data means Grafana has received no scrape status for 5 minutes: the collector is stopped or cannot export. No Rust telemetry means Rust is filtered out or has reported nothing for a day; it does not mean healthy.

panels.title: Rust last scrape age
panels.description: Age of the latest scrape-status sample Grafana received in the last day. The expected scrape interval is 60 seconds. Samples older than 120 seconds indicate delayed collection or export; the age keeps rising while the collector is stopped.

panels.title: Rust process memory
panels.description: Resident memory of the Rust process. This is not total Railway container memory; TypeScript does not export an equivalent process metric.

panels.title: Rust process CPU
panels.description: CPU seconds per second consumed by the Rust process. A value of 1 means one fully occupied CPU core.

panels.title: Rust resident memory
panels.description: Rust process metrics collected by Alloy over the private Railway network.

panels.title: Rust CPU usage
panels.description: Rust process metrics collected by Alloy over the private Railway network.
